claim: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3 with gcd(D)=1 for which there exist an integer B>=2, a nonempty finite set A of positive integers and a nonempty set C contained in D minus R, where R={B^a:a in A} is contained in D, such that sigma(R)=sum_{d in R}1/(d-1)>=1/2, gcd({B} union C)=1 and sigma(D minus (R union C))>=1, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k admit N(D,k,F) such that every integer n>=N is a sum of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once; coincident numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.

quadruple.statement: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3 with gcd(D)=1 for which there exist an integer B>=2, a nonempty finite set A of positive integers and a nonempty set C contained in D minus R, where R={B^a:a in A} is contained in D, such that sigma(R)=sum_{d in R}1/(d-1)>=1/2, gcd({B} union C)=1 and sigma(D minus (R union C))>=1, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k admit N(D,k,F) such that every integer n>=N is a sum of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once; coincident numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.
quadruple.stage: Finite positive and signed subsets of labelled integer pure powers, with common-radix exponent alignment, finite modular arithmetic and a disjoint reserve of positive powers.

shape.objects: Finite rigid sets D,A,C of integer parameters and a chosen radix B, with unbounded positive cutoffs, finite forbidden label sets and represented integers. Finite signed or positive supports are determined by their labels and have common extensions by disjoint union. Integer powers, finite sets, sums, products and gcd are defined in core Lean or Mathlib. Finite support choices may be random variables but no spread condition is recorded.
shape.quantifiers: For every finite D satisfying the explicit existential B,A,C condition, every positive k and every finite F, there exists N, and for every n>=N there exists a finite legal positive representation. These are universal leading quantifiers over finite arithmetic data, followed by eventual coverage and finite witnesses. No uncountable objects or all sets of reals are quantified over.
shape.target_quantity: A yes/no eventual-representation property under exact structural hypotheses, not an optimal exponent or numerical bound. An unspecified finite threshold N(D,k,F) settles the claim. The desired increment in the seed family is exactly one.
shape.ambient_structure: Order and integer arithmetic coexist. The actual operation is disjoint concatenation of pairs of finite positive supports with unit difference, increasing a represented interval length by one at each fresh pair. The inherited aligned-lattice argument supplies such pairs from R union C at every cutoff; the successor will reprove it. The reserve uses different base labels and is untouched. No probabilistic pair-dependence statistic, spread system or reflecting-category transport is recorded.
shape.symmetries: Relabelling preserves multiplicity. Disjoint support union preserves coefficient bounds, whereas overlapping union may reuse a label. Alignment at a common multiple of A gives an injective map of normalized radix weights back to R labels. Increasing D or decreasing k or F enlarges representation sets when the structural hypotheses remain true. No closed density-increment piece system is supplied.
shape.configuration: Exact equation n=sum of finite positive allowed labelled powers, every pair used at most once and equal numerical values retained separately. The amplification must preserve seed/correction versus reserve separation and all cutoffs and finite deletions. Restricting D, deleting selected seed labels or truncating an existing gadget can destroy the particular representation or structural mass hypothesis; fresh gadgets require a fresh cutoff. The configuration uses both arithmetic values and order.
shape.extremal_candidate: No optimal extremal family, constant, or rigidity claim is asserted. The proposed structural sufficient condition is not presented as necessary. Earlier fixed alphabets are comparison cases, not extremal candidates.
shape.finite_certificates: For fixed D,k,F,n, a finite representation is checkable. A signed-unit pair from R union C is the smallest positive integer increment and can be constructed by hand after any cutoff. Finite bounded support instances can in principle be encoded for a solver, but they are not an exhaustive reduction for the universal theorem. No mathematical process, uniform maximal exponent or finite-root computation is admitted.
shape.monotonicity: Adding allowed bases, lowering the cutoff or deleting fewer labels preserves positive representability and preserves an already chosen structural witness when its sets remain available. The smallest positive cutoff is one, but the theorem requires every positive cutoff. Raising required seed or reserve mass weakens a sufficient-condition theorem.
shape.uniformity_parameter: D, B, A, C, k, F and n vary without finite bounds. The proof may choose its cutoff-dependent alignment, gap, gadgets and threshold from D,k,F. The reserve gap must be fixed independently of the later number and supports of gadgets.
shape.proof_shape: A self-contained analytical proof candidate is written in moves/001-common-radix-reserve.md: signed-prefix interval induction, an injective aligned common-radix lattice, recurring-residue modular correction on disjoint base labels, a fixed positive mass-one reserve gap, and finite fresh-unit amplification prove the exact claim for every admitted input and cutoff. Independent result review is pending. No finite mathematical program, scalar optimization ledger or formal checker was used.
